t: You're looking at the statue of Robert Raikes in Victoria Embankment Gardens. Raikes is often regarded as the founder of Sunday schools. The sculptor Thomas Brock made it, and the Earl of Shaftesbury unveiled it on 3 July 1880, marking a hundred years since the first Sunday school opened. The critic Edmund Gosse thought it as good as anything of its kind in England. It has been Grade II listed since 1958. Brock is also known for the Victoria Memorial in front of Buckingham Palace.
